title: Walk out to Preikestolen
description: A flat 25-metre square of rock 604 metres above the Lysefjord, with no railing. Four kilometres each way over boardwalk and boulder.

title: Wedge yourself into Kjeragbolten
description: A boulder jammed in a crevice with a thousand metres of air below it. The walk in crosses three steep chain-assisted sections.

title: See the Fram and the Kon-Tiki in one afternoon
description: The ship that went furthest north and south, and the balsa raft that crossed the Pacific, on the same peninsula.

title: Walk the roof of the Oslo Opera House
description: White marble sloping straight out of the fjord, designed to be climbed. It is a public square that happens to be a roof.

title: Chase the aurora above the Arctic Circle
description: Three hundred and fifty kilometres inside the Arctic Circle and directly under the auroral oval. Chase inland if the coast is clouded.

title: Drive the Senja national tourist route
description: Norway's second largest island, with the peaks of Lofoten and none of the crowds. Tungeneset and Bergsbotn are the stops.

title: Stand at the North Cape at midnight
description: The northernmost point reachable by road in Europe, with the sun still up at midnight from mid-May to the end of July.

title: Walk the Bryggen wharf in Bergen
description: Leaning wooden Hanseatic warehouses on the harbour, burned and rebuilt on the same medieval foundations for six hundred years.

title: Ride the Flam railway down to the fjord
description: Twenty kilometres and 866 metres of descent on one of the steepest adhesion railways in the world, with a waterfall stop.

title: Walk the Besseggen ridge
description: A knife-edge between a green lake and a blue one, four hundred metres apart in height. Boat in, walk out.

title: Look for polar bears from a boat in Svalbard
description: Seventy-eight degrees north, where leaving the settlements without a rifle and a guide is illegal for good reason.

title: See the Vasa, raised whole from the harbour
description: A warship that sank on her maiden voyage in 1628 and was lifted intact in 1961. Ninety-eight per cent original timber.

title: Kayak the Stockholm archipelago
description: Thirty thousand islands, with the right of public access letting you camp on almost any of them for a night.

title: Ride the Stockholm metro for the art
description: Ninety of the hundred stations are decorated, several blasted out of bedrock and left raw and painted. A day ticket is the gallery fee.

title: Sleep in the Icehotel at Jukkasjarvi
description: Rebuilt every December from Torne river ice and melted back into the river each spring. Sleeping bags rated to minus twenty.

title: Walk a stretch of the Kungsleden
description: The King's Trail runs 440 kilometres through Swedish Lapland, with mountain huts a day apart and no roads for most of it.

title: Eat oysters straight off the Bohuslan rocks
description: Sweden's west coast grows flat oysters that are still hand-picked by divers. The season runs when the water is cold.

title: Cycle the walled town of Visby and beyond
description: Three and a half kilometres of medieval wall around a Hanseatic town, and raukar sea stacks along the coast north of it.

title: See the midsummer poles go up in Dalarna
description: Midsummer is the real national holiday. Dalarna does it hardest: flower crowns, a raised pole and dancing until it never gets dark.

title: Swim in the harbour at Islands Brygge
description: The harbour was clean enough to open to swimmers in 2002, in the middle of the city, and it is free.

title: Cycle Copenhagen on the Cykelslangen
description: An elevated bike-only bridge curving over the harbour. Nearly half of all trips to work in this city are by bicycle.

title: Look at the Louisiana sculpture park by the sea
description: A modern art museum built into a garden above the Oresund, with Calder and Giacometti on the lawn facing Sweden.

title: Walk Your Rainbow Panorama at ARoS
description: A circular glass walkway on the roof in every colour of the spectrum, so the whole city changes hue as you go round.

title: Stand where two seas meet at Grenen
description: The Skagerrak and Kattegat collide on a sandspit, and you can see the two wave trains meeting head on.

title: Watch the black sun over the marshes
description: Up to a million starlings murmurate over the Wadden Sea marshes at dusk in spring and again in autumn.

title: Walk to the lake above the ocean at Sorvagsvatn
description: An optical illusion where a lake appears to hang a hundred metres above the sea. Technically Danish, and utterly its own place.

title: Take the ferry to Suomenlinna fortress
description: A sea fortress across six islands, built by Sweden, taken by Russia, now a suburb you reach on a commuter ferry.

title: Sit in the Loyly public sauna on the sea
description: There are more saunas than cars in Finland. This one has a ladder into the Baltic, which is the point in February.

title: Sit in silence in the Kamppi Chapel
description: A curved spruce shell in the middle of the busiest shopping district, built for nothing but quiet. No services, no charge.

title: Cross the Arctic Circle at Rovaniemi
description: The line is painted across the ground at Santa Claus Village, and the reindeer and huskies are a short drive out of town.

title: Sleep under a glass roof in Lapland
description: Glass igloos built so you can watch the aurora from bed without your face freezing.

title: Ski or walk to a wilderness hut in Lapland
description: Open wilderness huts, free and unlocked, are a Finnish institution. Take your own food and leave firewood for the next person.

title: Look for a Saimaa ringed seal
description: Fewer than five hundred exist, all in this one lake system, landlocked since the last ice age.

title: Cycle between the Aland islands on free ferries
description: A Swedish-speaking autonomous province of Finland, with small inter-island ferries that cyclists ride at no charge.

title: Swim in a Reykjavik neighbourhood pool
description: Geothermal outdoor pools open all year at 29 degrees, with hot pots at 44. Wash properly first; they will check.

title: Walk between two continental plates at Thingvellir
description: The Mid-Atlantic Ridge surfaces here, and the Icelandic parliament met on it from 930 AD. The plates pull apart two centimetres a year.

title: Watch Strokkur go off every few minutes
description: The original Geysir gave the world the word and now rarely erupts. Strokkur next door goes up twenty metres every five to ten minutes.

title: Walk behind Seljalandsfoss
description: A sixty-metre fall with a path around the back of the curtain. You will get soaked, and the path ices over in winter.

title: Stand on the black sand at Reynisfjara
description: Basalt columns and sneaker waves that have killed people. Watch the sea, never turn your back on it, and stay well up the beach.

title: Cross the Fimmvorduhals pass
description: Twenty-five kilometres between two glaciers, over ground that was a lava field in 2010, linking Skogar to Thorsmork.

title: Bathe in the Myvatn nature baths
description: The northern answer to the Blue Lagoon, half the price and a fraction of the crowd, beside a lake full of pseudocraters.

title: Watch whales from Husavik
description: Skjalfandi bay has humpbacks most of the summer and blue whales some years. Old oak schooners run the trips.

title: Feel Dettifoss from the east bank
description: The most powerful waterfall in Europe by volume. The east side road is rougher and puts you closer to the edge.

title: Drive the Snaefellsnes peninsula
description: Called Iceland in miniature: a glacier-capped volcano, lava fields, black churches and Kirkjufell all on one loop road.

title: Walk inside a blue ice cave
description: Caves melt out of the glacier each winter and collapse each spring, so no two seasons are the same. Guides only.

title: Walk the medieval walls of Tallinn old town
description: The most complete medieval town centre in northern Europe, with twenty towers still standing and a working town hall from 1404.

title: Visit the Soviet-era Patarei sea fortress
description: A tsarist artillery barracks turned Soviet prison, left almost exactly as it was when it closed in 2002.

title: Walk the bog boardwalks of Lahemaa
description: Raised bogs with pools you can swim in, manor houses and erratic boulders left by the ice, an hour from the capital.

title: Look into the Kaali meteorite crater
description: A crater lake blasted out about 3,500 years ago by a meteorite that hit a populated island, and turns up in Baltic folklore.

title: Look up at Riga's art nouveau facades
description: Riga has more art nouveau than any city in Europe, and one street where every building competes with its neighbour.

title: Eat in the zeppelin hangars of Riga Central Market
description: Five German airship hangars moved here in the 1920s, now one of the largest markets in Europe.

title: Ride the cable car over the Gauja valley
description: An open cable car strung across the valley since 1969, with sandstone caves and three castles in the forest below.

title: Stand where the Baltic meets the Gulf of Riga
description: Two seas meeting over a sandbar, on a coast that was a closed Soviet border zone and so was never developed.

title: Cross into the republic of Uzupis
description: A self-declared artists' republic across a river in Vilnius, with its own constitution bolted to a wall in forty languages.

title: See the interwar modernist architecture of Kaunas
description: Built fast when Kaunas was the temporary capital between the wars, and world heritage listed for it in 2023.

title: Add a cross to the Hill of Crosses
description: Bulldozed three times by the Soviets and rebuilt each night. Over a hundred thousand crosses now, and you may leave one.

title: Climb the dunes on the Curonian Spit
description: Ninety-eight kilometres of sand bar between lagoon and sea, with drifting dunes that buried villages in the nineteenth century.
